messages:
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] High p99 latency spike detected in inference-runtime-prod on route /v1/generate (streaming). p95=1.1s, p99=7.2s, tail stalls observed. KV cache eviction rate and fragmentation both spiking. Paging: @alice (oncall)

alice (oncall): I'm on it. Looking at dashboards now — linking panel: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/abc123/inference-runtime?panelId=7  see p99 jump at 14:03 UTC. Any immediate customer tickets?

cs-rep: CS has 18 customer reports for streaming stalls >5s, 3 are on Dedicated instances. No data loss. Customers reporting repeated stalled tokens (client sees long silence then chunk).

ben (runtime): Confirming KV metrics: eviction_rate=612/s (norm 40/s), fragmentation_ratio=0.84, free_segments dropping quickly. Prefill write rate spike correlated with many short-prefix requests. Prefill hits dropping -> more decode misses -> more KV writes -> eviction loop. Logs tail:
```
[14:03:12] kv_cache.cpp:evict_key key=prefix_0x7d9a size=128KB reason=pressure
[14:03:12] scheduler.cpp:prefill queued=1200 inflight=96
[14:03:13] stream_handler.cpp:stall id=trace-5f3a client=acme-corp duration=6.2s
```

sarah (eng-ml): This looks like prefill vs decode imbalance. Short prompts cause aggressive prefill of KV pages for many unique prefixes; that crowds out hot KV entries used by longer streams. Two levers: throttle prefill for short sequences, or prefer decode-path (no prefill) when request len < N. Also consider adding small LRU buffer for hot prefixes.

mike (sre): Immediate mitigation plan (T-0):
1) Route ~30% traffic -> model-compact-v1 (lower KV footprint) to relieve pressure and reduce p99 while we stabilize.
2) Hotpatch runtime pool: increase kv-cache memory pool on pool-inference-1 from 24GB -> 32GB (temporary).
3) Toggle `prefill_threshold` from 0.9 -> 0.6 and reduce prefill_batch_size by 50% to lower write pressure.
4) Rolling restart of inference-worker pods (1 pod at a time) to clear fragmented segments after new pool size applied.
5) Enable eviction_protect for top-100 prefixes (protect hot keys).

ben (runtime): Executing step 2 & 3 now. Admin API calls:
```bash
# increase pool memory (admin API)
curl -X POST "https://runtime-admin.redwood/api/pools/pool-inference-1/resize" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"memory_gb":32}'

# update prefill config
curl -X PATCH "https://runtime-admin.redwood/api/config/prefill" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prefill_threshold":0.6,"prefill_batch_size":0.5}'
```

deploy-bot: Admin API resize request accepted, job id=job-9834. Prefill config patch applied by ben.

mike (sre): Starting rolling restarts. Will do 1 pod every 45s, circuit-check after each.

alice (oncall): Routing change for traffic split? Who's owning the route change?

mike (sre): I'll patch the router. Using canary config to route 30% to model-compact-v1: `curl -X POST https://router/api/traffic-split -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","splits":[{"model":"prod-default","weight":70},{"model":"model-compact-v1","weight":30}]}'`

ops-bot: Traffic split applied.

ben (runtime): Observability: eviction_rate down to ~180/s after pool resize + prefill patch. p99 trending down from 7.2s -> 1.8s within 5 minutes. Streaming stall counts decreased by ~60%.

cs-rep: Notifying impacted customers of mitigation. Suggested note: "We've applied emergency mitigations to reduce streaming stalls; engineering is investigating root cause and we'll follow up with details."

alice (oncall): Assigning severity P2. We're keeping the page open until p99 < 500ms and eviction_rate normalized for 30m. Ben will be primary for next 2 hours, Mike supporting restarts. I'll own postmortem and customer comms.

ben (runtime): Rolling restarts complete. Eviction fragmentation metric showed brief spike during restarts but settled. Current snapshot: p95=210ms, p99=420ms, eviction_rate=22/s, fragmentation=0.23.

sarah (eng-ml): Confirming ML-level fix candidates for follow-up: 1) prefill runtime heuristics: avoid prefill for requests < 32 tokens; 2) adaptive prefill backoff when eviction_rate > X; 3) small LRU hot-buffer for prefixes. I'll open RFCs and a short-term PR for heuristic change.

mike (sre): We'll schedule a capacity increase for pool-inference-1 in infra backlog (prod reserve) and add an alert rule for fragmentation_ratio > 0.6 to page instead of warn.

alice (oncall): Handoff: @ben primary for 2h monitoring, escalate to platform-incident if p99 > 1s again. @alice will prep postmortem outline and CS communication.

cs-rep: Customers updated. No active escalations.

incident-bot: Incident resolved -> mitigation in place; p99 reduced and eviction rate normalized. Incident severity P2. Follow-ups: postmortem, config RFC, capacity reservation.

alice (oncall): Closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions. Good work everyone :thumbsup:
